note: Hand-written element descriptions (summary <=110 chars, about 2-4 sentences, family). Loaded first by tools/fleet_viz/elements.py Describer; never regenerated.

families.Attention pipeline banks: Hardened register banks (one flop per bit, q <= d, no logic) used as wire-pipeline stages on the HBM accelerator's attention tiles. Each bank is a small macro with inputs on one edge and outputs on the opposite edge, so a long attention bus crosses the tile as bank -> straight wires -> next bank, and the clock tree sees one pin per bank instead of hundreds of flops.
families.Attention quad: The hardened building block of the 16-head attention tile: four one-head attention leaves around a shared register strip. Attention tiles compute QK scores and PV products over FP8/BF16 KV rows streamed from HBM.
families.Attention tiles (ATT): The attention tiles compute QK scores and PV products over FP8/BF16 KV rows read from HBM. The tile is split into a low and a high half-block, and its results travel to the stream-unit lanes over a relay chain.
families.Capture: The capture slab of the DeepSeek ROM die: it receives the gather's per-root FP32 results, rounds them to BF16, checks quota/position/range, packs row pairs and writes them into vector memory (VM), crossing from the stream clock to the slower serial VM clock. It is tiled into 8 root-group tiles under one control tile.
families.Clock and reset: Boot, clock and reset infrastructure of the HBM accelerator die: the production power-on/reset sequencer body and the per-endpoint reset collars that synchronise reset release into each clock domain.
families.Clock-domain crossings: Credit-flow-controlled clock-domain-crossing channels (Gray-pointer asynchronous FIFO) that move a wide word stream between unrelated clocks on the Qwen ROM die, preserving order and values and flagging credit violations as sticky faults.
families.Collective clocking: Clock and reset generation for the DeepSeek ROM die: the die PLL hard macro and the reset sequencer that roots the stream, serial and HBM clock domains.
families.Collective core: The DeepSeek ROM die's collective slab core: a 4-way tensor-parallel (TP4) collective engine that all-reduces (pairwise FP32 sums) and all-gathers partial results across the four ranks' dies, plus the vector-memory (VM) input/output queues and pass-through channels that feed the die-to-die lanes. The core is built as three abutted tiles (cb bottom/VM side, ce middle/engine, ct top), each further split into hardened sub-tiles with registered or credit-based seams.
families.Collective engine (COLL): The collective engine performs cross-die collectives for tensor/expert parallelism: all-reduce, all-gather, top-k merge, argmax merge, sub-group reduce with multicast and row gather from owner dies. It sends 545-bit flits over die-to-die SerDes links with credit flow control, link retry and idle insertion for plesiochronous clocks.
families.Collective links: Die-to-die lane tiles and adapters of the DeepSeek ROM die collective slab. Each lane is a reliable link layer (credits, replay buffer) plus a gearbox onto a 512-bit UCIe or board SerDes beat; dedicated lanes and endpoints carry multi-token-prediction (MTP) draft traffic so it never queues behind collective traffic.
families.Collector: The collector slab of the DeepSeek ROM die: it merges the result frames arriving from the four HBM-stack lanes into the single 512-bit lane to vector memory, forwarding only complete frames (frame-atomic, no arithmetic) and emitting one combined DONE per job.
families.Command processor (cmdproc): The command processor is the die's single in-order sequencer: it fetches program records, runs control steps (loops, fences, end of token, MTP control) and issues records to each engine's queue. Physically it is split into a north and a south band.
families.Constant ROM: Mask-ROM store of the model's per-layer constants (q/k norm tiles, RoPE cos/sin for 8,192 positions, output row scales) read by the stream unit through its 64-lane port. Built from 48 ROM macros arranged as 8 identical 8-lane group tiles.
families.Corridor and link stations: Pure one-cycle registered relay stages that carry the instruction/data corridor to the compute tiles and the 512-bit-each-way die links across the Qwen ROM die. Every boundary is register-to-register and flow control is credit-based, so long wires can be cut into hops without same-cycle handshakes.
families.DMA, loader and ingest: Blocks that move data between the host, HBM and vector memory: the loader (host command-processor window, boot load and the DMA engine front end) and the host ingest master that writes GPU-prefilled KV cache into HBM in the decode layout.
families.DS Engram: Engram is DeepSeek-V4.1's hashed lookup memory, whose tables live in HBM. The Engram slab hashes lookups, issues HBM row reads, checks and assembles rows, prefetches them and writes them into the vector memory for the layer that consumes them.
families.DS HBM controller boundary: The DeepSeek ROM die keeps per-user KV state in attached HBM; this slab is the die-side boundary to the HBM PHY. It is split into one tile per HBM pseudo-channel (PC) column plus a centre tile, so each clock tree spans a single column.
families.DS MTP (multi-token prediction): These blocks implement DeepSeek-V4.1 multi-token prediction (the DSpark drafter) across the die array: the head-die sequencer that accepts verified tokens and drives the draft chain, the seed path that feeds committed hidden rows to the drafter, the Markov draft head, and the link endpoints between them and the vector memory.
families.DS ROM MTP draft (DSpark): Blocks that run DeepSeek-V4.1's built-in multi-token-prediction drafter (DSpark) on the ROM array: seed projection, the Markov draft head, draft-die transport and the links between the head-die MTP sequencer and its neighbours.
families.DS ROM MTP rollback state: Speculative decoding writes draft tokens into position-indexed state; when the verifier rejects drafts these blocks restore the committed state. They compute the commit/squash range and keep ring buffers (token history, per-position control tables) sized for exact rollback.
families.DS ROM hyper-connection seed capture: DeepSeek-V4.1 keeps four residual copies per layer (hyper-connections, HC). For the DSpark multi-token-prediction (MTP) draft, the mean of these four copies at backbone layers 37, 38 and 39 is captured on each tensor-parallel rank, stored in ECC-protected SRAM and joined on the head rank to seed the drafter.
families.DS ROM lm_head: The vocabulary projection (lm_head) of the DeepSeek ROM die: weights sit in ROM macros, each read word feeds 16 BF16 multipliers so the multiply rate matches the ROM read rate, and per-element argmax results are merged into the next-token choice.
families.DS ROM sliding-window KV staging: The WINDOW stage of the DeepSeek ROM die's attention: KV rows for the sliding attention window arrive from HBM pseudo-channels into a four-bank staging buffer built from column macros, then are read four rows at a time into the attention row merge.
families.DS ROM stream-unit arithmetic: Fused 1.2 GHz floating-point pipelines of the DeepSeek ROM die's stream unit (SU), which handles the non-matmul vector math: softmax exponent and division, SwiGLU expert activation, and the hyper-connection post-mix. Tiles and half-rate (two cores on alternating clocks) variants are hardened sub-blocks of these units.
families.DS ROM wavefront token pipeline controll: Per-package controllers of the DeepSeek ROM die pipeline. They issue each user's positions through the layer-stage dies (wavefront issue of already-known prompt and draft tokens), receive results back, verify drafts and squash/re-issue on a mismatch.
families.DS host and ingest: The host block takes the host link's sector stream (KV rows, indexer keys, RoPE and Engram data) into the die and routes it to the HBM stack clients. It sits off the per-token decode path and handles loading and completion/credit reporting to the host.
families.DS selector / collector control: The selector slab runs the exact streaming top-k over attention scores arriving from the four HBM scan services, and the collector slab gathers their finished result frames. These blocks are the control tiles and command endpoints that tie those slabs to the stage sequencer and the vector memory.
families.DS stream unit (SU): The stream unit is the in-order engine that runs the fused full-width vector operations of the token path: RMSNorm and FP8 quantisation of q and kv (with RoPE), activation-quant banks, SwiGLU with routing weights, and attention softmax / normalisation. It reads wide rows from the vector memory and writes results back; the slab is built from hardened tiles on relay-station spines.
families.DS vector memory (VM): The vector memory is the die's banked on-chip SRAM scratchpad (8 Mb) that every engine on a layer die reads operands from and writes results to. Requests from all client ports take effect in a fixed global order with fixed read latency; the master is built from bit-sliced bank-group tiles with a front end (request side) and a back end (response side).
families.DS wavefront controller (WFC): The wavefront controller issues the token positions that are already known (prompt tokens and MTP drafts) through the pipeline of layer dies so they can be verified in parallel. The WFC kit on each stage die adds a token/draft store, a link bridge to the die-to-die collective, credit ports and transport into the vector memory and stage core.
families.DeepSeek MTP prefix path: The MTP (multi-token prediction) phase-2 prefix path on the DeepSeek ROM die: ordered transport of incoming rows, the exact prefix arithmetic and an FP32 adder array, then a publisher. It is split into four die-assembled hard tiles, each with its own clock tree, with every seam registered on both sides.
families.DeepSeek fused draft head: Hardware for the fused DSpark (MTP) draft head on the DeepSeek ROM die: the lm_head matrix-vector product, the Markov-row add and the argmax are fused on the matrix engine's output stream so each draft step needs no separate vector add or select. The head is built from SRAM lane leaves grouped into half-quadrants, a control view and a checked endpoint.
families.DeepSeek indexer scorer: The lightning-indexer score engine on the HBM accelerator scores cached keys against the query for DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse attention, to pick the top-k KV entries to attend to. Each score engine is built from 8-head chunks, and each chunk from identical one-head x one-key slices on systolic registered seams.
families.Die IO and collectives: The Qwen ROM die's external interfaces: link adapters in front of the UCIe and SerDes PHY macros, the host / KV-ingest block, and the collective engine that performs the tensor-parallel (TP4) all-reduce across the four dies of a package.
families.Die glue: Generated die-level glue of the DeepSeek ROM die: clock-domain crossing FIFOs and register stations that carry streams between columns, hubs and slabs.
families.Die interconnect stations: Forwarded-clock stations on the die's long buses (VM-root to matrix-engine activation multicast, matrix-engine to stream-unit result gather, and other spine chains). Each station re-times a slice of the bus every few hundred micrometres: forward stations pass data with its forwarded clock, launch stations start a forwarded segment from the local clock, mesochronous (meso) stations land it into the local clock through a small FIFO, multicast stations also tap the bus to local consumers, and gather stations merge local results into it.
families.Die-to-die link and collective: Link-layer blocks of the HBM accelerator's die-to-die (TU) links used by the collectives: the retry pipeline (ACK/NAK replay), the binding between the link PHY and the core, and the stage that publishes received collective results into vector memory (VM) with ECC.
families.Embedding ROM: The Qwen3-8B input-embedding table held in mask ROM on the die: thousands of code banks (64 vocabulary rows each) plus scale banks with per-row BF16 scales, reached through a root adapter and a chain of per-bank taps. A token id becomes one request; its code words stream back in order to the die IO bus.
families.Forwarded-link stations: Forwarded-clock repeater stations placed every few hundred microns along the die's long point-to-point chains (activation broadcast, return trunks, scan-service and die-link paths). Each registers one data slice plus its forwarded clock, adding one cycle per hop; 'stnh'/'stnv' are the horizontal/vertical-pin variants and the number is the lane width in bits.
families.Fused paths / quantiser: The fused-path engine runs the row norm, the DeepSeek hyper-connection norms and the block quantiser (FP8/FP4 quantise and dequantise) next to the stream unit.
families.HA2 die-to-die all-reduce link: HA2 is the HBM accelerator's direct die-to-die cut-through all-reduce network: each die has local ports to the other dies of its group and group ports, and each link direction carries credit-controlled flits through wire stages and a SerDes macro. These blocks are the true-credit sender/receiver queues and a transmit relay.
families.HBM accelerator MTP (DSpark): Blocks on the generic HBM accelerator that run DeepSeek-V4.1's DSpark speculative decode: the control loop issuing draft/verify passes to the compute (SM) cluster, the router top-K expert selector, the expert union of a multi-position pass, and the logit argmax epilogue.
families.HBM accelerator MTP block: Blocks of the MTP (multi-token prediction / speculative decoding) unit hfd_mtp on the HBM accelerator die: the accept unit that checks draft tokens against the verify pass, a shared scratch memory, and the fence that makes results visible to the host register-file service.
families.HBM accelerator links and collectives: Off-die communication on the HBM accelerator: the collective endpoint that sends partial results to and receives reduced results from the switch, and the link endpoint beside each SerDes with retry buffering and transmit banks.
families.HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path: Per-pseudo-channel logic between the HBM controller/PHY and the core clock domain: it classifies returned read beats (KV cache vs embedding), applies SECDED error correction to the 256-bit data + 32-bit check word kept in the HBM3E ECC side-band, decodes landed KV beats and keeps per-PC KV row requests in order.
families.HBM pseudo-channel controller: One JEDEC HBM scheduler per pseudo-channel (PC) on the Qwen ROM die: it turns descriptor / go / write commands from the KV and embedding streams into row (activate, precharge, refresh) and column (read, write) commands that respect DRAM timing. Commands arrive over an 8-entry credit boundary; payload storage, stream mapping and the PHY live in neighbouring blocks.
families.HBM stream service (svc) segments: The stream service (svc) is the HBM DMA/service layer that maps 32-byte sectors to HBM stacks and pseudo-channels and streams weight rows, KV rows and index keys to the engines. There is one per HBM stack (SW, SE, NW, NE); the SW design is reused mirrored for NW and SE for NE, and each is cut along x into roughly 1 mm segment blocks that talk through registered wire-stage chains.
families.HBM stream unit (SU): The stream unit is the HBM accelerator's vector unit: hundreds of identical lanes do element-wise and reduction work on streamed vectors (adds, multiplies, special functions such as sigmoid/SiLU), fed by a broadcast tree from a controller. Lanes are hardened once and replicated in the die's SU and SFU quarters.
families.HGI DMA engine: The DMA engine (unit 8) of the HBM accelerator die: it moves rows between HBM and the on-die vector memory with element-format conversion, appends KV rows, performs DeepSeek's KV write-back and the HBM write fence. It is split into a front (per-stack request split), the row mover, and a dedicated KV write-back engine built from hardened tiles.
families.HGI MTP control: Multi-token prediction (MTP, speculative decoding) control for the HBM accelerator die. The MTP master drives draft/verify rounds through the command processor; the merged argmax of each verify row comes back to it, and these blocks decide which drafted tokens are accepted.
families.HGI argmax: The local argmax unit (unit 7) of the HBM accelerator die: it finds the largest logit in this die's vocabulary shard and reports a global token id, which the collective engine then merges across dies.
families.HGI attention front end: Front-end logic of the attention tiles (ATT unit) on the HBM accelerator die. It decodes ATT.QK / ATT.PV records into attention-controller jobs and produces the ordered list of KV rows to read from HBM (a sliding-window ring followed by indexer-selected rows), plus the FP8 sector coding of KV data.
families.HGI block quantiser: The FUSED block quantise-dequantise path (FUSED.QDQ_FP8 / FP4) of the HBM accelerator die. It reads FP32 vectors from vector memory, applies block FP8 or FP4 quantise-dequantise exactly as the golden model does, and writes results back; the wide form streams several sectors per cycle over a VM lane group.
families.HGI collective engine (COLL): Pieces of the collective engine (COLL, unit 6), which performs cross-die operations: all-reduce, all-gather, top-k merge, argmax merge and row gather from owner dies. These blocks decode collective records, format row-gather requests and merge per-die top-k streams.
families.HGI command processor: The command processor (CP) of the HBM accelerator die under the HBM Generic Interface (HGI-1) contract. It fetches the per-token program of unit records from HBM, decodes them, resolves loops and indexed descriptors, and dispatches each record to the die's units (matrix, stream, DMA, attention, collective, ...), ending each token with its 18-bit output id.
families.HGI hyper-connections (HC): Hyper-connection (HC) hardware for DeepSeek-V4.1 on the HBM accelerator die: the HC mix projection and the fused HC pre-norm / post steps that combine the multiple residual streams around each layer.
families.HGI indexer / top-k (IDX): The indexer / top-k unit (IDX, unit 9) of the HBM accelerator die. IDX.TOPK selects the k largest entries (router experts, or up to 2,048 KV positions for DeepSeek sparse attention) using pipelined SRAM min-heaps; IDX.INDEX runs DeepSeek's indexer frame that produces the local KV selection.
families.HGI matrix engine (SM) support: Data movers around the 32 matrix engines (SM, matrix-vector units) of the HBM accelerator die. The x-load broadcasts activation vectors from vector memory into every SM's input store; the publication path collects SM result rows and writes them back to vector memory.
families.HGI record adapters: Thin decode-and-handshake adapters that turn one normative HGI-1 record from the sequencer into the existing command word of a unit (SM, SU, SFU, FUSED, HC, DMA, ARGMAX). They hold no datapath; they own ordering, retire and fault reporting for that unit.
families.HGI stream unit (SU): Controller of the stream unit (SU), the die's programmable vector pipeline for element-wise ops, reductions and exact fallbacks. It stages a record's operands from vector memory into local operand memory, runs the vector unit, and drains written results back to VM.
families.HGI vector memory (VM): The on-die vector memory (VM) of the HBM accelerator: a shared, banked SRAM (262,144 FP32 words) with per-word SECDED error correction that holds all activations. Units reach it through packet-client stations (up to 4 requests outstanding) or wide lane groups.
families.Hub clock-crossing end/start blocks: Registered FIFO blocks at the die's central hub where a long on-die link meets a hub block, each crossing a clock region. m2l blocks use a mesochronous FIFO (same-frequency link clock to the local tree), r2l blocks a 4:3 ratio CDC from the 1.2 GHz stream domain into the 0.9 GHz serial domain of the vector memory (VM), and l2r blocks the reverse (VM serial domain out to a 1.2 GHz stream lane).
families.Hub common-clock stations: Common-clock pipeline stations inserted on local buses between a hub end block and its hub slab when the bus is longer than one clock reach. Each is a flop-per-bit register stage on the local clock (one cycle).
families.Hyper-connections (HC): The DeepSeek hyper-connection unit mixes the residual streams around each layer (DeepSeek-V4.1's hyper-connection pre/post mixing). It is a quarter built from 88 identical hyper-connection post-mix lane tiles.
families.Indexer (IDX): The DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-attention indexer scores every cached index key against the quantised query and selects the top 512 KV positions per query, so attention reads only those rows from HBM. Index keys stream from each HBM stack's stream service to a per-stack scorer; scores are joined and sent to a per-die selector.
families.KV / window HBM service: Address and write units that place DeepSeek-V4.1 per-token KV, index-key and sliding-window rows in HBM pseudo-channels. The window ring is sized (256 slots) so that rows written speculatively during MTP verify can be rolled back exactly.
families.MTP control: Multi-token prediction (speculative decoding) control: drives the draft/verify loop, tracks the accepted token prefix and applies the stop conditions.
families.Matrix engine (SM) pieces: The SM (matrix engine) computes matrix-vector products, streaming weight rows from HBM against an activation vector (x) in BF16, FP8/FP4 block-dot or INT8 formats; the die has 32 SMs. The SM element (ot_hbm_accel_smh) is built as a physical hierarchy of small hardened pieces: a front (pins, channels, bulk copy, issue) cut into north/centre/south strips, per-leaf compute tiles with their x-store SRAMs and BF16/block-dot columns, and per-column back ends that combine and stream results back to the front.
families.Matrix-engine reduction and results: Blocks of the decode core's matrix-vector engine outside the weight tiles: the top levels of the FP32 adder reduction tree, the result path that moves result rows from the band slabs into the banked vector memory, and the core's sequencer/control partition.
families.Mesochronous FIFO: Clock-region crossings for the DeepSeek ROM die: the sender's forwarded clock and the receiver's clock share one reference (same frequency, unknown fixed phase), so a small ring buffer with guard bands crosses data without pointer synchronisers.
families.Native index pipeline: Blocks of the DeepSeek-V4.1 sparse-attention indexer path on the HBM accelerator: they carry query vectors to the top-k selector, pack and unpack the 15-slot candidate lists sent between dies, merge every die's sorted candidate list into one global order, and hash table-row IDs.
families.Qwen KV landing merge: KV rows landing on the Qwen ROM die's tiles are merged into full-width writes. The merge skid is a small credited queue on that path so a row is only launched when a seat is reserved for it.
families.Qwen KV-die near-HBM attention: The Qwen KV die computes decode attention next to HBM: row engines stream K and V rows from HBM, head tiles compute query-key scores and partial P.V sums, and the attention hub finishes the softmax (max, sum, reciprocal) and the final weighted sum returned to the ROM die.
families.Qwen KV-die write queue: On the Qwen KV die, new K/V rows arriving from the ROM die are queued and written into the HBM pseudo-channels (PCs) through per-PC landing crossings. These blocks split that write queue into a control tile, group tiles and per-PC leaf tiles so no single block carries thousands of pins.
families.Qwen ROM compute tile: The Qwen3-8B ROM die holds its INT8 weights in on-die ROM macros spread over ~1,536 replicated compute tiles. Each tile reads its ROM rows, multiplies them against the broadcast activation in lane slices, and also holds a slice of the KV cache fed through a per-tile landing hop.
families.Qwen ROM die link and clock-crossing sta: Blocks on the Qwen ROM die that move data across long distances or between clock domains: forwarded-clock relay stations on the die's long links and the per-HBM-pseudo-channel crossings between the KV memory clock and the core clock.
families.Qwen ROM-KV die-to-die link: Each Qwen ROM die is paired with a KV die that owns the HBM stacks holding the KV cache and runs attention near the memory. The die-to-die link carries queries, new K/V rows, attention results, embedding requests and control words between the two dies; these blocks are its two ends and their hardened buffer tiles.
families.Qwen decode core (whole-core block): Whole-core hardened blocks of the Qwen ROM die's decode core (controller with its engine interfaces) built as a single macro to close the core's own boundary timing and port behaviour.
families.Qwen near-HBM attention: Attention datapath for Qwen3-8B that sits next to the HBM holding the KV cache, attached to the Qwen ROM die package. The hub combines per-stack score rows into softmax weights (running max, Z normaliser tree, reciprocal) and the P.V weighted sum over values; the head row engine computes query-key dot products one KV row per cycle. Both were split into identical hardened sub-tiles with their own clock trees and registered seams.
families.Qwen sequencer / control: The Qwen ROM die runs a static program: the sequencer fetches each macro-instruction from the program store, adds per-token offsets (token row, RoPE row, KV slot, context length) and issues it to the matrix engine and stream unit. These blocks are that controller and its split pieces.
families.Qwen spine: matrix-engine reduction and: The spine of the Qwen ROM die collects the partial sums the compute tiles produce, reduces them through an adder tree, applies the per-row weight scales and finds argmax candidates. These blocks are the band lanes of that tree and the result-port groups that write results back.
families.Qwen stream unit (SU): The stream unit is the Qwen ROM die's 64-lane vector engine: it runs the element-wise work of a layer (norms, RoPE, softmax, SwiGLU via its special-function lanes) and packs K/V values for the KV cache. These blocks are the SU itself, its hardened lane tile, its local constant buffer and its KV packer.
families.Qwen tensor-parallel collective FIFOs: Qwen3-8B runs tensor-parallel across four ROM dies (TP4), so each layer ends in an all-reduce or all-gather. The collective FIFO is the local port between the sequencer's clock domain and the collective engine's clock domain, carrying 512-bit words each way under credit flow control.
families.Qwen vector memory (VM): The vector memory is the Qwen ROM die's shared banked SRAM for activations. It serves the matrix engine's activation (x) reads as conflict-free multi-bank beats and the row ports of the stream unit and link.
families.RMSNorm engine: The HBM accelerator's RMSNorm engine (fused fast path): reads the residual stream, gain and epsilon and produces the normalised BF16 vector, used for the pre-attention/pre-FFN norms and per-head QK-norm. For physical design it is split into replicated 8-lane group tiles plus a thin top holding the final reduction tree and rsqrt tail.
families.Router: The MoE router selects the top experts for each token from the router scores with a pipelined exact top-k selection.
families.S81 BF16 pair: The BF16-capable ROM compute pair of the S81 DeepSeek ROM die: weight families stored in BF16 run through these pairs (the default phase is FP8/FP4). The pair is built hierarchically from hardened macro-column tiles and a front tile with registered, abutted boundaries.
families.S81 die control and transport: Supporting blocks of the S81 DeepSeek ROM die outside the compute pairs: host ingest and dispatch, HBM pseudo-channel request muxing, head-group skew delays and the ROM field's reduction/gather roots and control spine.
families.S81 hyper-connection slab: The HC slab on the S81 DeepSeek ROM die computes DeepSeek-V4's hyper-connection (mHC) mixing: it keeps the resident multi-stream hidden state, applies the hc_post combine, RMS-norm (sum tree, divide, reciprocal sqrt) and activation quantisation. It takes commands from the die controller through an engine adapter and reads/writes vector memory (VM). It is built hierarchically: column sub-tiles in three chains, root tiles and a centre combine tile.
families.Scan-service IO hub tiles: The IO hub of each per-HBM-stack scan service, split into small tiles each placed at its own die pin group. They fan the incoming query stream out to the four quadrants and merge the quadrants' result streams (attention output, index results, outputs) back onto the die pins with forwarded clocks.
families.Scan-service job control: Command plumbing that lets the die controller drive the scan services as one engine: a die-level endpoint fans each job descriptor out to every scan-service slab and joins their completions, and a per-slab job tile gates query frames by job and watches result frames.
families.Scan-service slab tiles: Building blocks of the per-HBM-stack scan service slab (attention tiles plus the pooled indexer reader that stream KV/index data from HBM). They carry requests and responses between the HBM controller's pseudo-channel tiles, the four quadrants and the IO hub, one register per hop.
families.Special-function unit (SFU): The special-function unit runs the fused SwiGLU chain (gate activation times up-projection) for the MoE / FFN layers, reading and writing vector memory through its own packet client.
families.Stream unit (SU): The stream unit is the programmable vector pipeline whose 256-bit template configures multiply, add, special-function, reduce and round stages; RoPE, softmax, routing math and exact fallbacks run here. It is built from replicated lane tiles fed by result-gather buses from the matrix engines and by the attention root.
families.System control: The control plane of the Qwen ROM package: host interface, AXI4-Lite control/status registers, fault collection, reset sequencing and start/done coordination of the dies.
families.Token loop and MTP control: On-die control that runs autoregressive (AR) and multi-token-prediction (MTP) decode without a host doorbell per token: the host posts one job, each die runs the same deterministic token loop, and generated tokens are queued back to the host.
families.Vector memory (VM) halves: The vector memory (VM) is the HBM accelerator die's shared on-die scratch (262,144 FP32 words) holding activations, staged tables and id tables; engines reach it through request/response packets. It is built as four quadrants (NE, NW, SE, SW), each cut vertically into a west and an east half so every long pin face gets a full edge; the halves are joined by a registered seam bus.
families.W2 frame stations: Registered-boundary frame stations that hold one full frame (2,063-bit data + frame header + owner) and multicast it to NO = 2 or 3 branches, releasing it only after every branch returns a checked receipt. The large station is built hierarchically: word-group slice tiles (8- or 5-word groups) carry the protected payload, and a hub holds the shared phase/receipt/release control.

dsfd_cap_mtp_ep.summary: Capture-slab end of the MTP sequencer result link (grant-protocol sender) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_cap_mtp_ep.about: Small endpoint in the capture slab that sends the capture core's 512-bit RESULT flits to the head die's MTP sequencer receiver over the stationed die bus. It launches one flit per grant seen, so it stays correct over any relay-station count.

dsfd_capt_ctl.summary: Capture control tile: phase word, accept decision, constants for the 8 group tiles (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_capt_ctl.about: Central control tile of the tiled capture slab. It receives the phase word, decides acceptance, holds central state, drives one registered constant bus to each of the eight group tiles (with that tile's quota share precomputed), combines their fault/done, and crosses the status lane to the VM clock.

dsfd_capt_g2.summary: Single-clock capture group tile (16 roots), clock crossings moved to capt_x (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_capt_g2.about: Safe variant of dsfd_capt_grp: the same 16-root capture (BF16 rounding, checks, addressing) but entirely in the stream clock, with the pair packers and stream-to-serial crossings moved out into dsfd_capt_x.

dsfd_capt_grp.summary: Capture group tile: 16 roots of BF16 rounding, checks and VM row packing (x8) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_capt_grp.about: One of eight replicated tiles of the tiled capture slab, each handling 16 roots. Per root it rounds the gathered FP32 value to BF16, applies quota/position/range checks, computes the VM address, packs row pairs and crosses them from the stream clock to the serial VM clock; it also reports a registered fault OR and done AND to dsfd_capt_ctl.

dsfd_capt_x.summary: Capture clock-crossing tile: packs row pairs from stream to serial VM clock (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_capt_x.about: Small two-clock tile used with dsfd_capt_g2: it holds a capture group's pair packers and stream-to-serial ratio clock-domain crossings, so the group tile itself stays single-clock. Output feeds the vector-memory write lanes.

dsfd_cfifo.summary: Column entry FIFO: crosses the 564-bit activation stream into a ROM column (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_cfifo.about: Generated die glue, one per ROM column: the entry mesochronous FIFO that hands the 564-bit per-column lane stream (activations plus go/config bits) into the column's clock domain and up its slot-station chain. It is also the column's clock and reset root.

dsfd_coll_cb.summary: VM-side bottom tile of the collective core: VM in/out ports, output queue, lane 0/4 relays (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_cb.about: Bottom (south) tile of the three-tile collective core column. It holds the slab's vector-memory interface (f_vm records in, t_vm results out), the 16-deep sliced output queue that buffers the engine's packer words for VM, and the relay registers for lanes 0 (W0) and 4 (E0) between their lane tiles and the engine tile (dsfd_coll_ce) above it. Hardened variants cbf/cbq/cbq0/cbr are its sub-tiles (see dsfd_coll_cbh).

dsfd_coll_cbh.summary: Hierarchical VM-side collective tile composed from hardened cb sub-tiles (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_cbh.about: Wiring-only parent that rebuilds dsfd_coll_cb (same ports and function) from hardened sub-tiles: two lane-relay tiles (cbr, lanes 0 and 4 at the W/E faces), the f_vm pass-through tile (cbf, with the job endpoint) and five output-queue slices (cbq0, cbq x4) that each carry a slice of the t_vm result word. Each child has its own clock tree and registered seams.

dsfd_coll_cbj.summary: Collective core VM-side tile with the command endpoint that runs collective jobs (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_cbj.about: dsfd_coll_cb plus the collective command endpoint: it accepts a command (c_cmd) on its south face, lets the records of that collective message reach the engine under the job's descriptor, and reports done/status (c_done/c_st) when the job's last result leaves on t_vm. It is the VM-side tile master used in the collective slab; dsfd_coll_cbfj is its f_vm pass-through sub-tile.

dsfd_coll_ce.summary: Middle tile of the collective core: TP4 reduce/gather engine, receive FIFOs, VM queues (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ce.about: Middle tile of the collective core column. It holds the TP4 collective engine (pairwise FP32 all-reduce and all-gather over the four ranks), its receive FIFOs in SRAM, the six VM input queues, the packer that builds the result word sent down to the cb output queue, and the link credits for lanes 1, 2, 5, 6. It is being rebuilt as hardened sub-tiles: ces (engine lane slices), cef (remote receive FIFOs), cele/celp (lane links) and ceq (VM queues).

dsfd_coll_cef.summary: Receive FIFO tile for one remote rank's collective data (6 SRAM macros) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_cef.about: Sub-tile of dsfd_coll_ce (x3, one per remote source rank): the receive FIFOs for that rank's incoming collective data (2 parities x 3 SRAM macros) and their pull credit streams, fanned out to the four engine lane-slices.

dsfd_coll_cele.summary: Collective lane link tile for engine lanes 0-2 (credit tx/rx to the engine) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_cele.about: Sub-tile of dsfd_coll_ce for the engine-port lanes 0..2: face credit transmit/receive toward the lane tile, a transmit buffer with piggybacked credit counters, and the receive path into the remote FIFO tiles (dsfd_coll_cef).

dsfd_coll_celp.summary: Collective lane link tile for pass-through lanes 3-7 (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_celp.about: Sub-tile of dsfd_coll_ce for the pass-through lanes 3..7: moves words from the VM pass-through queue landing out to the lane, and lands incoming lane words into the four engine-slice landings, with credit links on every seam.

dsfd_coll_ceq.summary: Collective engine VM queue tile: six input queues, broadcasts and fault collector (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ceq.about: Sub-tile of dsfd_coll_ce. It takes VM records (f_vm) into six SRAM queues: queue 0 feeds the engine lane slices and queues 1-5 feed the pass-through lanes; it also broadcasts rank/enable/queue-pop control and collects faults. It is further split into dsfd_coll_ceq0 and dsfd_coll_ceqp.

dsfd_coll_ceq0.summary: Collective VM queue 0 tile with rank/enable control and fault collector (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ceq0.about: Part of the split VM queue tile of dsfd_coll_ce: holds queue 0 (the VM records that feed the collective engine's lane slices), the rank/enable control and the fault collector. Its siblings are five dsfd_coll_ceqp pass-through queue tiles, chained on a registered f_vm bus.

dsfd_coll_ceqp.summary: One pass-through VM queue tile of the collective engine (instanced x5) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ceqp.about: Part of the split VM queue tile of dsfd_coll_ce: one of five identical queue tiles (identity set by a strap) that buffer VM records bound for the pass-through lanes rather than the reduce engine. Fed from the registered f_vm chain shared with dsfd_coll_ceq0.

dsfd_coll_ces0.summary: Collective engine lane-slice 0: 4 FP32 lanes x 4 sources, credits and header (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ces0.about: One of four engine lane-slices of dsfd_coll_ce: the unmodified collective engine at 4 FP32 lanes x 4 sources with its local source FIFO and a slice packer. All slices run in lockstep on identical control; slice 0 additionally returns the credits and builds the result-word header.

dsfd_coll_cesn.summary: Collective engine lane-slices 1-3: 4 FP32 lanes x 4 sources each (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_cesn.about: The other three engine lane-slices of dsfd_coll_ce (slices 1..3), identical to slice 0 except that they do not return credits or build the header. Each reduces/gathers its 4 FP32 lanes of the word in lockstep with the other slices, with no cross-slice wires.

dsfd_coll_ck.summary: Die clock tile: PLL macro, reset sequencer and clock-output buffers (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ck.about: Clock tile of the collective slab: the die PLL hard macro (from a 100 MHz reference), the reset sequencer that releases the stream, serial and HBM domains after lock, and kept clock-output buffers. Its stream clock is the root clock of every collective tile.

dsfd_coll_ct.summary: Top tile of the collective core: relays for lanes 3 (W3) and 7 (E3) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_ct.about: Top (north) tile of the three-tile collective core column. It carries the registered relays (two-slot skids at each face) for lanes 3 (W3) and 7 (E3) between their lane tiles and the engine tile dsfd_coll_ce below.

dsfd_coll_lane_w.summary: Collective die-to-die link lane tile (west side): reliable link layer + SerDes gearbox (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_lane_w.about: One link lane tile of the collective slab (west-face pin plan; east lanes use the same RTL mirrored). It contains the reliable link endpoint (credits, replay buffer, 10 SRAM macros) and the gearbox that formats 552-bit flits onto the 512-bit UCIe or board SerDes beat, with registered skids toward the collective core. A link-up gate holds traffic until the peer's receiver has locked.

dsfd_coll_mtp_lane.summary: MTP adapter on a dedicated collective lane: token return, seed, accept events (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_mtp_lane.about: Adapter for the dedicated multi-token-prediction (MTP) lane W4 of the collective slab, abutting its own dsfd_coll_lane_w tile. It carries the head die's MTP sequencer traffic (token return, draft seed, accept/fault events) to the peer die with per-class end-to-end credits, so MTP never waits behind collective traffic.

dsfd_coll_p2_ep.summary: Collective-slab end of the P2 MTP draft links (grant-protocol tx/rx) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_p2_ep.about: Die-bus endpoint in the collective slab for the P2 draft path: transmitters for lane-1 words and transaction starts toward the P2 core, and a round-trip-sized receiver for its result rows. It uses the MTP grant protocol so data is correct over any number of relay stations; its partner is dsfd_p2_lnk.

dsfd_coll_p2_lane_ba.summary: P2 MTP draft lane adapter, die-B lane E4: receives expert-output words (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_p2_lane_ba.about: Instance of the P2 lane adapter (dsfd_coll_p2_lane) on MTP draft die A's UCIe lane E4 from die B: receives die B's 604-bit expert-output words in two beats and delivers them into a small register FIFO and grant-protocol sender onto the die bus. Abuts the mirrored E4 lane tile.

dsfd_coll_p2_lane_pa.summary: P2 MTP draft lane adapter, primary lane W4: sends result rows, receives starts (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_coll_p2_lane_pa.about: Instance of the P2 lane adapter (dsfd_coll_p2_lane) on MTP draft die A's primary board lane W4: transmits the 594-bit result row (two beats) and corrected/fault/done events to the primary, and receives the 101-bit transaction start and abort with end-to-end credits. Abuts the W4 lane tile.

dsfd_colt_lane.summary: Collector lane tile per HBM stack: frame parser, SRAM frame FIFO, credit sender (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_colt_lane.about: One of four collector lane tiles (one per HBM-stack lane, east pair mirrored). It captures the die lane at its pins, parses frames into a 2 x 256x256 SRAM frame FIFO, and forwards only complete frames word by word under credits to dsfd_colt_mrg, with a sticky fault sideband.

dsfd_colt_mrg.summary: Collector merger: frame-atomic merge of 4 stack lanes into one VM lane (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_colt_mrg.about: Merger at the centre of the collector slab. Per lane it lands words in a small credit-returning FIFO, then merges the four stack streams round-robin a whole frame at a time, combines the four per-stack DONEs into one, handles faults, and sends paced 512-bit words toward vector memory.

dsfd_ctrl_ctr.summary: Centre tile of the HBM controller boundary: resets, PHY reset and die status (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_ctrl_ctr.about: Sits between pseudo-channel tiles 15 and 16 of the HBM controller slab. Holds reset synchronisers, the HBM PHY reset, the sticky PHY out-of-range status, and merges the {fault, live} status chains from the two columns of PC tiles into the die status.

dsfd_ctrl_pc.summary: One HBM pseudo-channel tile of the HBM controller boundary (32 per die) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_ctrl_pc.about: One of 32 identical tiles, one per HBM pseudo-channel (PC) column at the PHY's pitch, that together with dsfd_ctrl_ctr form the HBM controller slab. Registers every request, write-data and read-response pin between the die and its PHY channel, and forwards the fault/live status chain to the centre tile.

dsfd_dw_ep_c.summary: Collector command endpoint: turns the collector's framed output into job done signals (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_dw_ep_c.about: Command endpoint tile for the collector slab (engine 6). Snoops the collector's framed word stream to the VM, skips raw data words, detects DONE/FAULT words, and reports job completion to the stage sequencer through a clock-crossing adapter and job queue.

dsfd_dw_ep_s.summary: Selector command endpoint: turns the selector's output word stream into job done signals (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_dw_ep_s.about: Command endpoint tile for the selector slab (engine 5 of the stage controller's adapter). Snoops the selector's word stream to the VM, detects DONE/FAULT words, and returns job completion to the stage sequencer through a clock-crossing adapter and job queue.

dsfd_engram_c.summary: Engram slab: hashed table lookup in HBM, row assembly and prefetch into vector memory (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_engram_c.about: Engram engine (engine 10) of the layer die that hosts Engram. Combines a command endpoint, the lookup element (hash, address, HBM row requests, CRC), the row sink (assembles BF16 rows) and an SRAM prefetch buffer. Built entirely of hardened tiles.

dsfd_host.summary: Host / KV-ingest block: loads KV rows, indexer keys and raw data from the host link (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_host.about: Die master of the host ingest block. Receives host-link writes in its own clock domain and turns them into sector writes on the die (compressed and window KV rows, indexer keys, raw). Write-only and off the decode path.

dsfd_host_native.summary: Host interface with visibility fence: reports completion only after writes truly land (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_host_native.about: Wraps dsfd_host with the native host ABI. Holds each host completion until the sector writes it covers are physically acknowledged, and keeps finite completion and credit state toward the host.

dsfd_host_sd.summary: Splits the host sector stream into per-HBM-stack writes (KV, RoPE, Engram) (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_host_sd.about: Sits after dsfd_host. Classifies each sector as KV, RoPE or Engram and routes it to the right HBM stack client: KV interleaved across the KV stacks, RoPE to the KV stacks, Engram to the Engram slab. Returns credits to the host and drops bad words with a sticky fault.

dsfd_hstnh_515.summary: 515-bit common-clock register station on a hub-local bus, end block to slab (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_hstnh_515.about: A one-cycle, flop-per-bit pipeline station on the local clock, used where a 515-bit local bus from a hub end block to its hub slab is too long for one hop (e.g. the bus from the SW scan service's collector entry block into the banked collector). Three instances on the die; plain rising-edge flops, same function as the generated glue station.

dsfd_l2r_vr_512x1__hq_SW.summary: Sends the query vector from vector memory to the SW scan service, serial-to-stream crossing (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_l2r_vr_512x1__hq_SW.about: l2r start block beside the vector memory (VM): takes the 512-bit query word from the VM's 0.9 GHz serial domain and launches it as a 1.2 GHz stream lane. The lane runs through forwarded-link stations to the SW HBM stack's scan service, where the matching hqe_SW entry block receives it.

dsfd_l2r_vr_564x1__hx_E.summary: Launches the activation (x) broadcast from vector memory, E half of the die (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_l2r_vr_564x1__hx_E.about: l2r start block for the east die half, placed in the vertical channel east of the hub: takes the 564-bit x lane stream (two activation sub-vectors plus control bits) from the vector memory's serial domain and launches it on the 1.2 GHz forwarded x trunk. The trunk fans out up and down the half and along every tier channel to the ROM weight column frames.

dsfd_l2r_vr_564x1__hx_W.summary: Launches the activation (x) broadcast from vector memory, W half of the die (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_l2r_vr_564x1__hx_W.about: l2r start block for the west die half, placed in the channel west of the hub: takes the 564-bit x lane stream (two activation sub-vectors plus control bits) from the vector memory's serial domain and launches it on the 1.2 GHz forwarded x trunk. The trunk fans out up and down the half and along every tier channel to the ROM weight column frames.

dsfd_m2l_raw_512x1__hl_E0.summary: Receives die-link E0 traffic into the collective block, mesochronous crossing (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_m2l_raw_512x1__hl_E0.about: m2l end block beside the collective slab for link 0 on the die's east edge (each edge has one UCIe and three board SerDes links). 512-bit raw receive data arrives from the link macro through forwarded-link stations; this block moves it into the collective's local clock and hands it to the collective (the inter-die communication engine).

dsfd_m2l_vr_512x1__hco_SW.summary: Entry FIFO taking SW scan-service attention partials into the banked collector (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_m2l_vr_512x1__hco_SW.about: m2l end block beside the banked collector (N band): receives the 512-bit attention-partial stream from the SW HBM stack's scan service over a forwarded-link chain and crosses it into the collector's clock region. Its 515-bit local output is staged to the collector by dsfd_hstnh_515 stations.

dsfd_m2l_vr_512x1__hix_SW.summary: Entry FIFO taking SW scan-service index scores into the selector (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_m2l_vr_512x1__hix_SW.about: m2l end block beside the selector (S band): receives the 512-bit indexer-score stream from the SW HBM stack's scan service over a forwarded-link chain and crosses it into the selector's clock region for top-k selection.

dsfd_m2l_vr_512x1__hqe_SW.summary: Entry FIFO delivering the query vector into the SW scan service (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_m2l_vr_512x1__hqe_SW.about: m2l end block beside the SW HBM stack's scan service: receives the 512-bit query stream launched by the hq_SW start block at the vector memory and crosses it into the scan service's clock, feeding its q input.

dsfd_m2l_vr_68x10__hr_E0.summary: Gathers ROM column return results, E half tier 0, into the gather block (DeepSeek ROM die)
dsfd_m2l_vr_68x10__hr_E0.about: m2l end block at the end of the return trunk for tier 0 of the east die half: 10 68-bit lanes, one per weight column in that tier (66-bit return-tree root word plus fault/busy). It crosses the forwarded return lanes into the local clock and feeds the hub's gather block, which assembles the matrix-vector results from the ROM field.
