The host writes descriptors and config into it; it dispatches records to every unit and reports the token result.

ot_hgi_cp_mtp_pinreg.summary: Registered boundary collar between command processor and MTP master (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_cp_mtp_pinreg.about: The MTP side of the command processor's MX1 collar with every crossing registered: valid/ready channels go through 2-entry pin FIFOs, job and level inputs land in pin flops, outputs leave from flops. It connects the CP to hgi_mtp_native (command, emit, backend and host-record channels) at +1 cycle per crossing.

ot_hgi_dma_front.summary: DMA front: splits loads per HBM stack and feeds VM wide write lanes (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_front.about: Takes eligible DMA LOAD moves, splits them across the per-stack HBM service lanes and streams the returned data into the vector memory's wide lanes, sized to the DMA load bandwidth budget. Sits between the HBM service side and VM, beside the mover.

ot_hgi_dma_kvw.summary: KV write-back engine: copies KV rows from vector memory to HBM (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_kvw.about: The DMA mover's KV write-back engine (DMA.KVWB_DS for DeepSeek's KV window ring, and other raw VM-to-HBM row copies). Reads VM over a wide lane group into a 2-bank SRAM buffer and drives 4 per-stack HBM write streams, about 2 sectors per cycle.

ot_hgi_dma_kvw_core.summary: Core tile of the KV write-back engine: control, buffer SRAMs, HBM write streams (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_kvw_core.about: Hardened part of ot_hgi_dma_kvw: the decision logic, the two buffer macros, the per-stack HBM write streams and lane rings. Pairs with two ot_hgi_dma_kvw_hold tiles that capture the VM read lanes.

ot_hgi_dma_kvw_hold.summary: Read-hold tile of the KV write-back engine (16 VM read lanes, 2 per engine) (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_kvw_hold.about: Hardened hold tile of ot_hgi_dma_kvw: registers 16 VM read lanes in pin flops, holds landed sectors in 32 entries and hands them to the core over registered bank ports. Two instances per engine, beside ot_hgi_dma_kvw_core.

ot_hgi_dma_mover.summary: DMA row mover between HBM and vector memory with format conversion (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_mover.about: Full-rate row mover behind ot_hgi_dma_record: executes the 227-bit move word (source/destination space, element format, base, strides, m x n shape) sector by sector between HBM service channels and VM, converting element formats, plus the HBM write fence.

ot_hgi_dma_mover_el.summary: DMA row mover as its own element, with the KV write-back engine split out (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_mover_el.about: The DMA row mover as the die runs it when the KV write-back engine is a separate element: the sector engine reads VM through the packet client, while the wide VM read group belongs to ot_hgi_dma_kvw. Its outline is sized to its real interface.

ot_hgi_dma_record.summary: Record adapter: decodes DMA LOAD/STORE/FENCE records onto the DMA mover's command port (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_dma_record.about: Unit 8: turns DMA.LOAD, STORE, FENCE and KVWB_DS records into the DMA mover's row-move command (source/destination space, format, base, strides, shape) and its fence port. Decode and handshake only, between the command-processor sequencer and the engine.

ot_hgi_fused_record.summary: Record adapter: decodes FUSED records onto the fused fast-path's command port (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_fused_record.about: Unit 4: front of every FUSED op (HC pre-norm, row norm, HC post, softmax, FP8/FP4 quantise-dequantise); it maps each onto existing engines, e.g. ROW_NORM as a gain load by the DMA mover plus a stream-unit micro-sequence. Decode and handshake only, between the command-processor sequencer and the engine.

ot_hgi_hc_lane.summary: Lane slice of the fused HC engine (32 lanes) for HC post / pre-norm (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_hc_lane.about: Hardened replicated lane of the fused HC engine ot_hgi_hc_eng (32 lanes), which runs the HC post and HC pre-norm steps in one pass. VM-side inputs are pin-flopped, outputs registered, with an SRAM write FIFO per lane.

ot_hgi_hc_lane_ll.summary: Lane-local HC engine lane: HC post / pre-norm on its own VM bank (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_hc_lane_ll.about: Lane-local rebuild of the HC engine: each of the 32 lanes runs HC post (8 pipelines) and HC pre-norm (mix, x buffer, chunk sums, scale) on its own VM bank, with registered inputs and outputs. Built from 8 ot_hgi_hc_lane_sl slices.

ot_hgi_hc_lane_sl.summary: One of 8 slices of a lane-local HC engine lane (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_hc_lane_sl.about: Hardened element slice of ot_hgi_hc_lane_ll (8 per lane), splitting the lane's logic into smaller tiles with their own clock trees.

ot_hgi_hc_record.summary: Record adapter: decodes HC.HC_MIX records onto the hyper-connection unit's command port (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_hc_record.about: Unit 10: maps the DeepSeek hyper-connection mix record onto the HC projection engine's command and HBM weight window; the output is the 24-word mix (pre, post, combination) in VM. Decode and handshake only, between the command-processor sequencer and the engine.

ot_hgi_hc_unit.summary: Hyper-connection unit: DeepSeek HC mix projection from VM residuals (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_hc_unit.about: HC unit body behind ot_hgi_hc_record: stages the residual from VM into the projection engine's local x memory, streams the layer's HC weights from HBM once for all positions, and writes the mix outputs back to VM.

ot_hgi_idx_index_w.summary: DeepSeek indexer frame (IDX.INDEX) on 32 VM wide lanes (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_idx_index_w.about: Throughput redesign of the IDX.INDEX frame adapter: reads candidate scores over a 32-lane VM wide group, keeps up to 32 candidates per cycle and writes the compacted local KV selection back to VM, for DeepSeek's sparse-attention indexer.

ot_hgi_idx_topk_w8_cluster.summary: 8-wide top-k as one cluster: hub logic plus 8 hardened heap tiles (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_idx_topk_w8_cluster.about: Physical composition of the production 8-wide IDX.TOPK: pipelined hub logic (lane relays, status tree, compare and merge relays, registered SRAM ports, result skid) with 8 ot_hgi_topk_heap_tile instances on its edges.

ot_hgi_mtp_accept18.summary: MTP accept endpoint widened to 18-bit token ids (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_mtp_accept18.about: The plain accept endpoint of the MTP path in its HGI-1 18-bit token form (legacy DeepSeek width is the default; routed builds enable 18 bits). It sits on the MTP side of the command processor and handles the accepted-token results of verify rounds.

ot_hgi_mtp_core18.summary: MTP controller core with 18-bit token ids, generic-interface width (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_mtp_core18.about: The registered full-shape MTP core widened to the HGI-1 18-bit token id (the lineage intended for Qwen MTP; DeepSeek's 17-bit form remains the default). Adds a registered reset release so its reset tree can be timed over several cycles.

ot_hgi_quant_decode.summary: FP8/FP4 block quantise-dequantise arithmetic, one 32-value beat per cycle (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_quant_decode.about: Arithmetic core of FUSED.QDQ: takes one complete beat of 32 FP32 values with its record header and produces the quantised-dequantised result (FP8 E4M3, FP4 with E8M0 or E4M3 scales) and fault flags. Used inside the transport and wide quantiser engines.

ot_hgi_quant_vm_transport_p.summary: Pipelined transport moving quantiser sectors between vector memory and arithmetic (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_quant_vm_transport_p.about: Pipelined form of the quantiser's VM transport: issues sector reads and writes through a VM packet client, keeps a result FIFO in one SRAM and feeds ot_hgi_quant_decode. Same ports and semantics as the original transport, only retimed.

ot_hgi_quant_wide.summary: Wide FP8/FP4 quantise-dequantise engine on a VM lane group, 4 sectors/cycle (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_quant_wide.about: FUSED.QDQ wide engine: reads 4 sectors (one 32-value beat) per cycle from a VM lane group, runs ot_hgi_quant_decode at one beat per cycle and writes results back, with per-lane response FIFOs and a registered boundary. Replaces the slower packet transport for throughput.

ot_hgi_quant_wide_h.summary: Hierarchical wide quantiser: read/write quad tiles, decode tile and SRAM (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_quant_wide_h.about: Physical hierarchy of ot_hgi_quant_wide with identical behaviour: 8 hardened read quads (ot_hgi_qw_rq), 8 write quads (ot_hgi_qw_wq), one decode tile (ot_hgi_qw_dec) and a result SRAM, joined by registered seams.

ot_hgi_qw_dec.summary: Decode tile of the wide quantiser: registered FP8/FP4 QDQ arithmetic (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_qw_dec.about: Sub-tile of ot_hgi_quant_wide_h holding the ot_hgi_quant_decode arithmetic with registered inputs and outputs. Takes beats from the read quads and sends results toward the write quads.

ot_hgi_qw_rq.summary: Read-quad tile of the wide quantiser: 4 VM read lanes and response FIFOs (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_qw_rq.about: One of 8 read quads of ot_hgi_quant_wide_h on the VM lane-group read side: per-lane request flops, response FIFOs and a gather register that assembles beats for the decode tile.

ot_hgi_qw_wq.summary: Write-quad tile of the wide quantiser: 4 VM write lanes (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_qw_wq.about: One of 8 write quads of ot_hgi_quant_wide_h on the VM lane-group write side: takes the registered result beat and drives 4 lanes' write requests, returning write credits and done events.

ot_hgi_seq.summary: Record sequencer: fetches, decodes and dispatches the per-token program records (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_seq.about: Fetches program records from HBM into an SRAM prefetch ring, decodes headers and operand descriptors, runs nested CTL.LOOP bodies, computes effective addresses (including indexed descriptors read from VM tables) and issues each record to its unit after its wait mask. CTL.FENCE waits for all units and HBM writes; CTL.END produces the token id, range-checked to 18 bits and the vocabulary.

ot_hgi_sfu_record.summary: Record adapter: decodes SFU.GLU records onto the SwiGLU special-function unit's command port (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_sfu_record.about: Unit 3: decodes the SwiGLU record into one vector op on the special-function unit's stream-unit op port; same issue, ordering and fault logic as the SU adapter. Decode and handshake only, between the command-processor sequencer and the engine.

ot_hgi_sm_pub_slice.summary: Publication slice: writes 4 matrix engines' result rows back to vector memory (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_sm_pub_slice.about: One of 8 hardened slices of ot_hgi_sm_pub, the SM result publication path: collects result rows from 4 SMs, coalesces them into sector writes in local SRAM and drains them to VM. A parent block relays commands and merges the slices' VM clients.

ot_hgi_sm_record.summary: Record adapter: decodes SM.MATVEC records onto each matrix engine's command port (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_sm_record.about: Unit 1: splits a matrix-vector record across the per-SM command ports of the die's 32 SM elements (rows per SM, format, x and descriptor words), working with the SM x-load and publication peers. Decode and handshake only, between the command-processor sequencer and the engine.

ot_hgi_sm_xload.summary: Loads activation vectors from vector memory into all 32 SMs' input stores (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_sm_xload.about: Peer of ot_hgi_sm_record's x port: reads activation rows from VM through packet clients and broadcasts them over the existing x-write port into every matrix engine's x store in the SM fragment layout. In the FP8/FP4 path it also quantises x on the fly.

ot_hgi_su_ctl.summary: Stream-unit controller: stages VM operands, runs the vector op, drains results (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_su_ctl.about: Die body of the stream unit: record from ot_hgi_su_record, then stage the op's VM operands into local operand memory through one VM packet client, run the unchanged vector unit on local addresses, and write changed words back to VM before retiring.

ot_hgi_su_ctlw.summary: Wide stream-unit controller: stages/drains operands over 32 VM wide lanes (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_su_ctlw.about: Production wide form of ot_hgi_su_ctl: staging and draining use the VM wide lanes (about 1 KB per cycle) instead of the packet client, writing back only dirty words. Same ordering, faults and stream paths as the narrow controller.

ot_hgi_su_ctlw_slice.summary: 8-lane slice of the wide stream-unit controller, chained with its neighbours (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_su_ctlw_slice.about: Hardened 8-lane slice of ot_hgi_su_ctlw; slices are stacked and linked by registered nearest-neighbour connections that pass descriptors forward and combine done/overflow status back. Lane logic is the same as the flat controller.

ot_hgi_su_record.summary: Record adapter: decodes SU.VOP records onto the stream unit's command port (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_su_record.about: Unit 2: decodes an SU.VOP record (header, SU template, operand descriptors) into the stream unit's existing 670-bit vector op word; no arithmetic or data path. Decode and handshake only, between the command-processor sequencer and the engine.

ot_hgi_topk_heap_tile.summary: One SRAM min-heap tile of the 8-wide top-k unit (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_topk_heap_tile.about: Hardened heap of the 8-wide IDX.TOPK: one pipelined min-heap with pin flops, a credit-based op port, registered SRAM write ports and local reset/clear. Eight sit around the hub in ot_hgi_idx_topk_w8_cluster.

ot_hgi_vm_btile.summary: Vector-memory bank tile: lane queues, ECC encode/decode and SRAM ports (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_vm_btile.about: Hardened bank tile of the vector memory: per-lane pin flops and SRAM queues, client select and SECDED encode, registered macro inputs, read capture and decode, and responses back to clients. Replicated across the VM banks inside the die's VM unit.

ot_hgi_vm_unit.summary: On-die vector memory: banked SRAM with SECDED and client stations (HBM accelerator)
ot_hgi_vm_unit.about: Vector memory block body: the banked core of SRAM macros with per-word SECDED, plus one station per packet client (up to 4 outstanding, in-order responses) and wide lane groups. Every compute unit reads and writes activations here; error and protocol faults go to the command processor.

ot_lkep_sub.summary: Sub-channel tile of the SerDes link endpoint: retry buffer, TX bank and credit relays (HBM accelerator).
ot_lkep_sub.about: One of 3 identical tiles of the link endpoint hfd_lk_ep that sits beside each of the 9 SerDes. It holds the link-level retry buffer, a transmit bank, pin queues and the relay chains to the shared glue, with every seam registered.

ot_meso_fifo_w512d4.summary: 512-bit, 4-deep mesochronous clock-crossing FIFO between same-frequency clock regions (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_meso_fifo_w512d4.about: Hardened view of ot_meso_fifo at width 512, depth 4, with every input registered at the pin. It moves 512-bit words from one clock region's forwarded link clock into the receiving region's clock tree, with a credit-based ready.

ot_meso_fifo_w512d8g1.summary: 512-bit, 8-deep mesochronous clock-crossing FIFO in the die configuration (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_meso_fifo_w512d8g1.about: Hardened view of ot_meso_fifo at width 512, depth 8 with the die's guard and 16-credit settings, pin-registered. It is the variant used on the die for crossings between same-frequency clock regions.

ot_mtp_commit.summary: MTP commit/rollback sequencer: kept length, next anchor, squash range and epoch (DeepSeek ROM die)
ot_mtp_commit.about: Runs on the head-die sequencer side after each verify pass. Given the anchor position, number of drafts and number accepted, it computes how many positions to keep (q+2+a), the next anchor, the squash range and a new epoch, which drive rollback of every position-indexed speculative state ring.

ot_mtp_hist_ring.summary: Engram token-history ring (last 16 tokens) with exact rollback after draft rejection (DeepSeek ROM die)
ot_mtp_hist_ring.about: Holds the raw token ids that DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram layers hash (the last four tokens of each position) in a 16-slot ring. Draft tokens are written speculatively; on rejection the commit pointer restores the committed history so the Engram hash unit reads correct tokens.

ot_mtp_hist_ring_p.summary: Pipelined, pin-registered version of the Engram token-history ring (DeepSeek ROM die)
ot_mtp_hist_ring_p.about: Registered successor of ot_mtp_hist_ring with the same function: requests are captured at the pins, bank selection and tag compare are registered, and a streamed decrementing position replaces the subtract before the read mux. One token per cycle, with two extra cycles of first-read latency.

ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path.summary: Draft-die path that sums expert partial rows in exact reference order (DeepSeek ROM die)
ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path.about: Selected MTP draft-die (P2) transport-plus-arithmetic path: ECC-protected rows tagged with expert id arrive over an ordered transport into SRAM, are summed as an exact prefix (+0, then each expert in fixed order) and are re-published as native FP32 output words. Streams one word per cycle.

ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path_hub.summary: Hub (top level) of the two-level hierarchical build of the draft-die prefix path (DeepSeek ROM die)
ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path_hub.about: Parent level of ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path split into a two-level hierarchy: the hub holds the top-level control and connects separately hardened sub-blocks of the draft-die expert-sum path, instead of placing the whole path as one flat block.

ot_nhb_pbst.summary: Per-stack beat store of the Qwen near-HBM attention hub: buffers KV beats in two SRAMs (Qwen ROM die).
ot_nhb_pbst.about: One of 4 identical tiles, one per HBM stack. It registers the stack's input pins, stores arriving beats in 2 x 128x256 SRAMs and holds a 512-bit capture register that the hub parent reads by page/position address. Part of the near-HBM attention hub (ot_qwen_nearhbm_attn_hub_t), which turns per-stack attention scores into softmax-weighted value sums; the parent holds decode, max, Z control, reciprocal and P.V control.

ot_nhb_pvlg.summary: P.V lane-group tile of the Qwen near-HBM attention hub: 4 lanes of probability x value sums (Qwen ROM die).
ot_nhb_pvlg.about: One of 4 identical tiles. Each covers 4 lanes and does the adds and the multiply by 1/Z that form the softmax-weighted sum of value vectors (P.V), with pin flops on inputs and registered outputs/fault. Part of the near-HBM attention hub (ot_qwen_nearhbm_attn_hub_t), which turns per-stack attention scores into softmax-weighted value sums; the parent holds decode, max, Z control, reciprocal and P.V control.

ot_nhb_zh.summary: One head of the softmax normaliser (Z) sum tree in the Qwen near-HBM attention hub (Qwen ROM die).
ot_nhb_zh.about: One of 4 identical tiles, one per head. It stores the head's Z tree nodes (128 x 32-bit) and runs its 4 tree adders, with replicated read-address copies and one-hot writes decoded locally; the masked root sum leaves registered to the parent, which takes its reciprocal. Part of the near-HBM attention hub (ot_qwen_nearhbm_attn_hub_t), which turns per-stack attention scores into softmax-weighted value sums; the parent holds decode, max, Z control, reciprocal and P.V control.

ot_p2h_arith.summary: Arithmetic core of the MTP prefix path: prefix computation with SRAM storage and codecs (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_p2h_arith.about: Takes ordered rows through a pin FIFO and runs the prefix arithmetic (3 SRAMs, encode/decode), passing results out through an output FIFO; uses the separate 16-lane adder tile for FP32 adds. One of the four tiles of the MTP phase-2 prefix path (ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path); the hub tile handles start/abort, context ownership and output.

ot_p2h_fadd16.summary: 16-lane FP32 adder array for the MTP prefix path (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_p2h_fadd16.about: Pin flops followed by 16 pipelined FP32 adders (8-cycle latency) with registered outputs, serving the prefix arithmetic tile. One of the four tiles of the MTP phase-2 prefix path (ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path); the hub tile handles start/abort, context ownership and output.

ot_p2h_xport.summary: Ordered-transport tile of the MTP prefix path: lane FIFOs and an SRAM row reorder buffer (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_p2h_xport.about: Receives two input lanes through pin FIFOs and puts rows in order using a 9-SRAM ordered-rows buffer, then hands them on through an output FIFO. One of the four tiles of the MTP phase-2 prefix path (ot_mtp_p2_prefix_path); the hub tile handles start/abort, context ownership and output.

ot_qkh_ktree.summary: Upper levels (4-7) of a head's query-key adder tree plus score scaling, Qwen near-HBM head (Qwen ROM die).
ot_qkh_ktree.about: Takes the 16 level-3 partial sums from the lane8 tiles and adds them in the original pairing through tree levels 4-7, applies the score scale and ORs the lane faults. Part of the hierarchical near-HBM head row engine (ot_qwen_nearhbm_head_hs), which computes query-key scores for 4 heads, one KV row per cycle.

ot_qkh_lane8.summary: 8 dot-product lanes plus adder-tree levels 1-3 of one Qwen attention head (Qwen ROM die).
ot_qkh_lane8.about: Identical hardened tile (lane position set by a strap) holding lanes 8t..8t+7 of a head and the first three levels of the K-score adder tree, with its own reset relay and registered seams; its partial sums feed ot_qkh_ktree. Part of the hierarchical near-HBM head row engine (ot_qwen_nearhbm_head_hs), which computes query-key scores for 4 heads, one KV row per cycle.

ot_qkvd_fbuf8.summary: Hardened shallow (8-deep) flop link buffer tile for the die link ends (Qwen KV die)
ot_qkvd_fbuf8.about: A hardened 8-deep flop buffer tile used in the die-to-die link ends, organised as 8 slices of 66 bits each with its own control copy behind pin flops. It replaces part of the flat flop buffers so the link parent keeps only link logic.

ot_qkvd_kv_end.summary: KV-die end of the ROM-to-KV die link, built over hardened buffer tiles (Qwen KV die)
ot_qkvd_kv_end.about: The KV die's end of the die-to-die link: it receives queries, K/V rows, control and embedding requests from the ROM die and sends back attention results, embedding data and HBM-control words. Its deep link buffers are the hardened ot_qkvd_sbuf and ot_qkvd_fbuf8 tiles.

ot_qkvd_rom_end.summary: ROM-die end of the ROM-to-KV die link (queries/KV out, attention results in) (Qwen ROM die)
ot_qkvd_rom_end.about: Sits between the ROM die's stream unit, vector memory and sequencer faces and the UCIe die-to-die macro. It sends queries and new K/V rows to the KV die, returns attention results into vector memory, forwards embedding requests and returns their data, and carries sequencer control words, all credit flow-controlled.

ot_qkvd_sbuf.summary: Hardened deep (64) link buffer tile: SRAM body + registered head queue for the die link (Qwen KV die)
ot_qkvd_sbuf.about: A hardened buffer tile for the die-to-die link ends: up to 64 words of 528 bits held in an SRAM macro plus flops, with a registered write stage and an 8-deep head queue. The link parent keeps occupancy; this tile keeps order and data with its own clock tree and reset relay.

ot_qwen_link_fwd_cx_station.summary: Forwarded-clock relay station: re-times a long on-die link hop on a forwarded clock (Qwen ROM die)
ot_qwen_link_fwd_cx_station.about: A relay station on the die's long links: it captures data on the falling edge of the received forwarded clock and passes on an inverted copy of that clock with the data, so each hop is centre-aligned instead of a zero-cycle hold race. Chained to carry words across the die.
ot_qwen_link_fwd_cx_station.family: Qwen ROM die link and clock-crossing stations

ot_qwen_nearhbm_attn_hub_p.summary: Attention hub: softmax max/sum/reciprocal and final P.V levels, times 1/Z (Qwen KV die)
ot_qwen_nearhbm_attn_hub_p.about: Finishes attention for the near-HBM stack: the running max, the softmax sum (Z) tree, the reciprocal, the last P.V reduction levels and the final scaling by 1/Z. Its result goes back over the die link to the ROM die's vector memory.

ot_qwen_nearhbm_ectl_h.summary: Engine control tile of a near-HBM attention row engine: HBM row fetch and FIFOs (Qwen KV die)
ot_qwen_nearhbm_ectl_h.about: The control tile of a near-HBM row engine: it issues KV row requests to HBM, keeps many rows outstanding in SRAM-backed row FIFOs, and feeds the landing data in stream order to the engine's head tiles.

ot_qwen_nearhbm_head_h.summary: Head tile of a near-HBM attention engine: q.K scores, scaling and partial P.V (Qwen KV die)
ot_qwen_nearhbm_head_h.about: One head tile of a near-HBM row engine: 128 lanes, the K reduction tree, score scaling, local P.V lanes and the query rows. It turns K/V rows from HBM into scores and partial weighted sums sent on to the aggregator.

ot_qwen_rom_core_core_kv_banked.summary: Whole decode-core controller block with full-width banked KV interface (Qwen ROM die)
ot_qwen_rom_core_core_kv_banked.about: The Qwen decode core's controller hardened as one block in its full-width configuration with a banked KV interface and a registered flush. It issues the static program to the engines and drives their gated engine clock; used as the whole-core boundary block.

ot_qwen_rom_core_core_p.summary: Whole decode-core controller block with completion (done) handshake (Qwen ROM die)
ot_qwen_rom_core_core_p.about: A variant of the Qwen decode core controller hardened as one block, including the completion/done handshake and the gated engine-clock output. It plays the same role as core_kv_banked: issuing the static decode program and pacing the engines.

ot_qwen_slab_port_group_s14_die.summary: One result-port group of the spine slab: scale ROM, FP32 post-scale, argmax leaves (Qwen ROM die)
ot_qwen_slab_port_group_s14_die.about: One result-port group of the matrix-engine slab. It crosses the block's result words into the spine clock, looks up per-row weight scales in its scale ROM banks, applies them with FP32 multipliers, writes the scaled results and computes the first levels of the argmax compare tree for the output head.
ot_qwen_slab_port_group_s14_die.family: Qwen spine: matrix-engine reduction and result ports

ot_qwen_stream4_cdc_pc.summary: Per-HBM-pseudo-channel clock crossing between the KV stream controller and core clock (Qwen ROM die)
ot_qwen_stream4_cdc_pc.about: One of 128 per-pseudo-channel (PC) clock-domain crossings of the STREAM4 KV service: gray-pointer async FIFOs carry landing data from the HBM-side stream controller clock to the core clock and write data back the other way, with credit return. Variants are alternate constraint/outline builds.
ot_qwen_stream4_cdc_pc.family: Qwen ROM die link and clock-crossing stations

ot_s81_bf_front.summary: Front tile of the S81 BF16-capable ROM pair: stream input and control ahead of the columns (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_bf_front.about: Generated from the native BF-capable S81 pair (ot_s81_bf_native). It holds the pair's front end that receives the BF16/FP8 activation stream and go signal and drives the hardened column tiles (ot_v41_bf_col); it adds no cycles over the native pair.

ot_s81_hc_comb.summary: Centre combine tile of the S81 hyper-connection slab: sequencer, final sum tree, norm tail (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_hc_comb.about: Holds the engine adapter, root sequencer and VM slots, the final sum-tree rungs, the norm scalar tail (divide, reciprocal sqrt) and activation quantisation, plus the centre column chain's root. Sits under the centre pin tile between the two outer column roots. Part of the hierarchical HC slab (dsfd_sp_hc), which applies DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection mixing and normalisation.

ot_s81_hc_cpin.summary: Centre pin tile of the S81 hyper-connection slab: commands, VM reads, y input (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_hc_cpin.about: Owns the centre third of the slab face: the controller-clock command/done pins, vector-memory (VM) read slots, status pins and the y valid/ready with credit counting. Every pin lands in a flop and crosses to the combine tile below in one more register. Part of the hierarchical HC slab (dsfd_sp_hc), which applies DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection mixing and normalisation.

ot_s81_hc_crootr.summary: Chain-root half of an outer S81 hyper-connection column root: chain subtrees and relays (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_hc_crootr.about: South half of a split outer column root (west or east chain): it holds the chain's sum subtrees and forward relays, requests each beat's y slice from ot_s81_hc_crooty, and sends VM write slots north. Part of the hierarchical HC slab (dsfd_sp_hc), which applies DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection mixing and normalisation.

ot_s81_hc_crooty.summary: Pin and y-FIFO half of an outer S81 hyper-connection column root (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_hc_crooty.about: North half of a split outer column root: owns the slab pins over its third of the face (its chain's y slice and four VM write slots) and the y slice FIFO, handing slices to ot_s81_hc_crootr below. Used once per outer chain (west and east). Part of the hierarchical HC slab (dsfd_sp_hc), which applies DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection mixing and normalisation.

ot_s81_hc_ctile.summary: Column sub-tile of the S81 HC slab: resident hidden state, hc_post and norm lanes (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_hc_ctile.about: Identical tile replicated in three column chains; each owns one octet (or half-octet) of element groups: the resident hidden state h in BF16, its hc_post combine lanes writing back in place, and norm lanes feeding partial sums up the chain to the roots. Part of the hierarchical HC slab (dsfd_sp_hc), which applies DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection mixing and normalisation.

ot_s81_hc_rtile.summary: Single root tile of the S81 hyper-connection slab (earlier layout), sequencer + norm tail (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_hc_rtile.about: Earlier one-tile root of the HC slab, later split into pin, combine and column-root tiles. It held the engine adapter, pin flops, y skid buffer, root sequencer and VM slots, the norm tail (128-leaf sum tree, divide, reciprocal sqrt) and 4 activation quantisers. Part of the hierarchical HC slab (dsfd_sp_hc), which applies DeepSeek-V4 hyper-connection mixing and normalisation.

ot_s81_head_delay8x32.summary: 8-cycle, 256-bit delay element used to build the S81 head-group lane skew (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_head_delay8x32.about: One paired-lane skew element (exactly eight cycles, 256 state bits), hardened once and replicated: the head's per-lane skew is composed from j%8 copies so lanes arrive staggered as the head pipeline expects.

ot_s81_host_dispatch.summary: Dispatches host-sector words to per-class consumers with shared credits (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_host_dispatch.about: Takes 290-bit host-sector ABI words with 8 shared credits and routes each word to exactly one branch by class (e.g. RoPE tables, Engram), accumulating returned credits and returning one credit per cycle upstream. Part of the die's host ingest path.

ot_s81_ingest_visibility_fence.summary: Host-ingest fence: counts host write completions, passes them to the engine clock (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_ingest_visibility_fence.about: Counts host-write completions from the memory controller, crosses a held snapshot into the engine clock with a toggle/ack handshake, and keeps an 8-entry completion queue and credits, so engines only read host data once it is written. Range/overflow checks raise a fault.

ot_s81_native_pc_mux_plain.summary: Request mux for one HBM pseudo-channel: arbitrates decode, KV, RoPE, Engram traffic (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_native_pc_mux_plain.about: Endpoint for one HBM pseudo-channel (PC) controller port: four sources (decode, host KV, RoPE, Engram) each hold eight queue credits, decode has priority and the others alternate. One transaction per PC keeps write-data identity; output pins are registered.

ot_s81_pq_ret_root_cam_p.summary: Root reduction CAM: pairs sibling partial-sum packets and adds them for the ROM field (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81_pq_ret_root_cam_p.about: Pipelined final-reduction root: incoming partial-sum tree packets are matched against held entries by tag in a CAM; when a sibling is found the pair is added and its parent packet issued, one candidate per cycle. One of 128 root owners at the end of the ROM field's reduction tree.

ot_s81ph_root_tile.summary: Region root tile of the S81 gather column, chained to pass results north (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_s81ph_root_tile.about: One of 128 region roots of the gather (dsfd_sp_gather), built as abutted tiles: a column of tiles is a registered south-to-north shift chain that carries each tile's result and its neighbours' results to the gather's capture, so no wide routing channel is needed.

ot_su12_ctl16h.summary: Stream-unit controller: issues lane ops; reductions every other cycle (HBM accelerator).
ot_su12_ctl16h.about: Controller of the c12 stream unit (16 lanes per group) that issues operations to the lanes; reduction steps are issued only on every second cycle to pair with the half-rate reduction tree.

ot_su12_light.summary: Plain vector lane of the stream unit (no special functions), replicated 192x per quarter (HBM accelerator).
ot_su12_light.about: Lane kind 0 of the c12 stream unit: FP multiply/add datapath with registered memory-word and gather inputs and registered outputs. 192 copies sit in the die's hfd_su quarter, fed by broadcast chains.

ot_su12_sfu.summary: Stream-unit lane with a special-function unit (sigmoid/SiLU), replicated in the SFU quarter (HBM accelerator).
ot_su12_sfu.about: Lane kind 1 of the c12 stream unit: the plain lane plus a sigmoid chain (exp, denominator, divide). 32 copies sit in the die's hfd_sfu quarter. Its sigmoid chain can be a separate hardened sub-tile (ot_hdc_v41x_sfu_chain).

ot_v41_bf_col.summary: One ROM macro column of the S81 BF16 pair as a hardened tile with registered boundary (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_v41_bf_col.about: Generated from the q-element's MAC column: weight ROM macros plus multiply-accumulate lanes producing partial sums. Every input, including clock-gate enable and reset, is captured at the boundary, so the column runs exactly one cycle behind the element; outputs leave its own registers. Composes with ot_s81_bf_front into the BF pair.

ot_v41_pqc_spine_screen.summary: Control spine of the ROM field: phase/stream ROMs sequencing ops and broadcasts (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_v41_pqc_spine_screen.about: Timing-screen top of the field spine (ot_v41_spine_pqc_w17w10) with all ports registered as on the die: it reads its phase and stream ROMs, issues operations, drives the activation broadcast and talks to the vector-memory ports and region roots. Composed of sub-tiles (ot_pqc_t_*, an activation quantiser ot_dsrom_aq12t).

ot_v41_rom_elem_q_qxpq_w10.summary: Weights-in-ROM compute element (q pair): ROM macros, MAC lanes, weight-word walker (DeepSeek ROM die).
ot_v41_rom_elem_q_qxpq_w10.about: The q-variant ROM element: reads the model's weights from ROM macros, walks the compressed weight words and multiply-accumulates against the broadcast activation stream, sending partial sums toward the field's reduction tree. This version adds the field-spine handshake signals for the PQ field phase.

qfd_cdc1024.summary: 1,024-bit credit-based clock-crossing tile (x4) replacing the multi-channel IO crossing FIFO (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_cdc1024.about: One hardened single-crossing channel of 1,024 bits, used four times in place of the earlier five-channel, four-clock IO crossing FIFO block. Words enter with credits in the writer's clock, cross through a Gray-pointer asynchronous FIFO and leave on the reader's clock only when a downstream credit is held.

qfd_chead.summary: Column-head station: splits the instruction/data corridor into north and south branches (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_chead.about: Same station design as qfd_cst, configured as a column head (64 copies): besides the onward corridor and tile tap it drives a second registered corridor copy so the corridor splits north and south, and combines the readies of all branches.

qfd_coll_xfifo.summary: Clock-crossing port between the sequencer and the TP4 collective engine (all-reduce/gather) (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_coll_xfifo.about: Carries 546-bit words (tag, mode, data) from the sequencer to the collective engine and 516-bit result words back, across the two clock domains with credit flow control. A credit gate only lets the sequencer send a word when the return path can hold every result it can produce (N for all-gather, 1 for all-reduce).

qfd_coll_xfifo_b.summary: Second instance/outline (b) of the sequencer-to-collective-engine clock-crossing port (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_coll_xfifo_b.about: The b variant of qfd_coll_xfifo: the same sequencer-to-collective-engine port with credit-gated return buffering, for a second die slot or outline.

qfd_coll_xfifo_l8.summary: Collective-port variant with both crossing FIFOs in dual-clock register-file macros (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_coll_xfifo_l8.about: A rebuild of the collective port whose two clock-crossing FIFO bodies are dual-clock register-file macros instead of flops, with a deeper return queue sized for all-reduce throughput. Same function as qfd_coll_xfifo.

qfd_coll_xfifo_l8_b.summary: Second outline (b) of the macro-based collective clock-crossing port (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_coll_xfifo_l8_b.about: The b variant of qfd_coll_xfifo_l8: the macro-based sequencer-to-collective-engine clock-crossing port, for the second die slot or outline.

qfd_crom_g.summary: Constant-ROM group tile: 6 ROM macros serving 8 lanes of norm, RoPE and scale constants (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_crom_g.about: One of 8 group tiles that make up the 48-macro constant ROM read by the stream unit's 64-lane port. Holds per-layer q/k norm tiles, RoPE cos/sin for 8,192 positions and output row scales; does lane address decode, capture and output. This version has a fixed lane base.

qfd_crom_gs.summary: Constant-ROM group tile with a lane-base strap so one design serves all 8 groups (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_crom_gs.about: Same function as qfd_crom_g (6 ROM macros, 8 lanes of the constant ROM) but the group's lane base is a registered static strap input, so a single hardened tile can be placed for all 8 groups instead of one netlist per group.

qfd_cst.summary: Corridor station: one registered stage of the 508-bit instruction/data corridor with a tile tap (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_cst.about: Placed in every tile corridor (over a thousand copies). It delays the corridor's downstream word (instruction, go and 128-bit data) by one cycle, drives a separate registered tap into the adjacent compute tile, and returns a registered AND of the downstream ready signals upstream.

qfd_ctrl_emb_00.summary: PC 0 HBM scheduler plus a static-row port for embedding-table reads/boot writes (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_ctrl_emb_00.about: The per-pseudo-channel scheduler (the lookahead-head form) extended with a static-row command queue used for the input-embedding region stored in HBM. Static entries arrive with their own credits and are marked on the column command, so the PC port can tell embedding traffic from KV-cache traffic.

qfd_ctrl_pc_00.summary: JEDEC HBM command scheduler for pseudo-channel 0 of 32; issues row/column commands (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_ctrl_pc_00.about: One of 32 identical controllers, one per HBM pseudo-channel (this is PC 0). It accepts descriptor, go and write commands behind an 8-entry command-credit boundary and emits row commands (activate / precharge / refresh) and column read/write commands with DRAM timing enforced, in the HBM controller clock domain. It does not hold payload data or contain the PHY; read data returns through the PC port and clock-crossing blocks.

It accepts descriptor, go and write commands behind an 8-entry command-credit boundary and emits row commands (activate / precharge / refresh) and column read/write commands with DRAM timing enforced, in the HBM controller clock domain. It does not hold payload data or contain the PHY; read data returns through the PC port and clock-crossing blocks.

qfd_ctrl_protected_00.summary: Dual-replica fail-closed HBM scheduler for PC 0 that zeroes commands on replica mismatch (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_ctrl_protected_00.about: A protected version of the PC 0 scheduler: two copies of the JEDEC scheduler run in lockstep and every command, credit and busy output is forced to zero if they disagree or halt. It covers a single upset in sequential state; outputs leave from registers so DRAM command spacing is unchanged.

qfd_ctrl_ready_00.summary: PC 0 HBM scheduler variant: lookahead command-queue head, registered bank-write eligibility (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_ctrl_ready_00.about: A timing-improved form of the per-pseudo-channel JEDEC scheduler (same function and ports as qfd_ctrl_pc_NN), built for PC 0. The command FIFO head is presented one step early and bank write eligibility is registered, shortening the critical decision paths without changing cycles.

qfd_ctrl_shift_00.summary: PC 0 HBM scheduler variant with an oldest-first shift write queue (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_ctrl_shift_00.about: Another implementation of the per-pseudo-channel JEDEC scheduler for PC 0, functionally identical to qfd_ctrl_pc_NN. The write queue is an oldest-first shift structure that also stores each entry's bank one-hot, removing decode logic from the write-ready path.

qfd_emb_pc_00.summary: Composite for PC 0: embedding-capable controller, PC port and three-FIFO clock crossing (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_emb_pc_00.about: Combines, in the controller reservation, the embedding-capable pseudo-channel scheduler, the PC port (read classification and ECC) and three clock-crossing FIFOs between the HBM controller clock and the core clock. KV command and raw landing interfaces stay separate from the embedding path; the PHY supplies the 288-bit protected codeword.
qfd_emb_pc_00.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_emb_pcport.summary: Per-PC HBM port: sorts read beats into KV vs embedding and SECDED-corrects embedding data (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_emb_pcport.about: Sits beside each pseudo-channel controller between the controller/PHY and the PC's core-clock crossing. It tracks every issued read in an in-order class FIFO, passes KV beats unchanged to the KV landing path, and decodes embedding beats (256 data + 32 check bits, four SECDED(72,64) words) into corrected data with correctable/uncorrectable flags. It also ECC-encodes the static embedding boot-load writes.
qfd_emb_pcport.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_emb_pcport_kvw.summary: PC port variant that also ECC-encodes KV-cache write data into 288-bit codewords (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_emb_pcport_kvw.about: The qfd_emb_pcport block built with KV write encoding enabled: in addition to embedding handling, it encodes KV-cache write data into 288-bit codewords (256 data + 32 SECDED check bits) for the HBM3E ECC side-band, matching the layout the KV landing correction expects.
qfd_emb_pcport_kvw.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_emb_pcport_kvw2.summary: PC port variant encoding KV writes at the die's real write timing for the HBM ECC side-band (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_emb_pcport_kvw2.about: The qfd_emb_pcport block with the KV write side-band provider at the die's actual timing: KV write data arrives from the per-PC STREAM4 clock-crossing completion one edge after the write column command, and the encoded 288-bit write data is presented to the PHY two edges after that column.
qfd_emb_pcport_kvw2.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_embed_code_bank.summary: One embedding ROM code bank: 64 vocabulary rows (4,096 x 512-bit) in two ROM macros (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_embed_code_bank.about: Leaf of the embedding ROM; the die instantiates thousands of these. Two mask-ROM macros hold bits 0-255 and 256-511 of each code word; reads are credit-controlled and a downstream seat is reserved before each read. Mutable metadata is complement-checked; the ROM payload itself has no ECC. Variants are the parent tile and its retained-netlist form.

qfd_embed_ingress_code.summary: Input-capture island at an embedding code bank's request pins (address, valid, credit) (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_embed_ingress_code.about: A small separately hardened block holding the request capture flops of an embedding code bank: address, valid and credit are registered at the pins with complement copies for checking. It is not an extra pipeline stage. Variants differ only in pin/outline arrangement (numeric vs padded).

qfd_embed_ingress_scale.summary: Input-capture island at an embedding scale bank's request pins (address, valid, credit) (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_embed_ingress_scale.about: Same design as the code-bank ingress island, placed at a scale bank's request pins: it registers address, valid and credit with complement copies. Variants differ only in pin/outline arrangement (numeric vs padded).

qfd_embed_scale_bank.summary: Embedding ROM scale bank holding per-row BF16 scales for the vocabulary (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_embed_scale_bank.about: Three instances cover the vocabulary, each with 65,536 BF16 row scales used to dequantise the embedding code words. Same credit protocol as the code banks; row, credit and pointer metadata is complement-checked and fail-stops publication. Variants are the parent tile and its retained-netlist form.

qfd_io_collective.summary: TP4 all-reduce engine: rank-ordered FP32 sum of activation vectors across the 4 dies (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_collective.about: The Qwen ROM die's collective engine for tensor parallelism over the four dies of a package. It folds the partial FP32 vectors from each rank in a fixed rank order (so results are bit-exact on every die), with credit-based ports and registered boundaries. The hierarchical build composes four hardened lane slices (qfd_io_collective_fs) with FIFOs.

qfd_io_collective_fs.summary: Hardened 4-lane slice of the all-reduce engine's FP32 fold datapath (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_collective_fs.about: A hardened lane slice (4 lanes, 128 bits) of qfd_io_collective: the pipelined FP32 adders and alignment for the rank-ordered all-reduce fold. Four slices are placed inside the collective engine parent.

qfd_io_emb_root.summary: Root of the embedding ROM: decodes token requests to banks and returns 512-bit words in order (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_emb_root.about: Single block at the embedding ROM's die face. It queues requests from the die bus, decodes each code-word or scale-row address to a bank, column and tap, issues one request every two cycles to one bank at a time so responses return in order without tags, and registers the merged 512-bit response back to the die IO.

qfd_io_emb_tap.summary: Per-bank tap on an embedding ROM column chain: forwards requests, returns bank responses (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_emb_tap.about: One beside each embedding bank: a registered hop on the column's request chain (down) and response chain (up). It captures requests addressed to its bank in a 4-entry FIFO, launches them on the bank's credits and puts the bank's response on the up chain.

qfd_io_host.summary: Host / KV-ingest block: writes host-sent KV-cache tiles and embedding boot data into HBM (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_host.about: Receives data from the host over the board SerDes host link and writes it into HBM: QKV (KV-cache) tiles and the raw embedding-table boot load. It is write-only, with per-lane KV corner-turn buffers (SRAM banks) that reorder host data into HBM layout, and runs on its own host and ingest clocks.

qfd_io_serdes.summary: SerDes link adapter: same credited flit adapter as UCIe, for the 112G SerDes PHY (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_serdes.about: The same link-adapter design as qfd_io_ucie, configured for the 112 Gb/s SerDes x12 PHY macro with a wider receive buffer. It converts between the die bus's credit protocol and link flits with sequence numbers and credit returns.

qfd_io_ucie.summary: UCIe link adapter: wraps die-bus words into credited, sequenced flits for the UCIe PHY (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_io_ucie.about: Digital logic between the die bus (valid + word + credit) and the UCIe x64 PHY macro. On transmit it buffers words and launches flits carrying payload, credit return and a sequence number whenever the link is up; on receive it buffers incoming payloads and returns credits to the far side.

qfd_kv_merge_skid.summary: 8-deep credited skid queue merging landed KV rows into full-width writes (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_kv_merge_skid.about: A finite merge-side queue on the KV landing path: the row sender spends a credit before launching a row, the queue holds up to 8 full 512-bit payloads with masks, and a credit returns only when the merged write leaves.

qfd_kvc_decode_map_pc.summary: Per-PC KV-cache beat decoder with built-in address map, computing the expected sector (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_kvc_decode_map_pc.about: Full-width version of the KV landed-beat decode that also performs the address map: given a counter from the PC ordinal owner, it computes the expected sector itself (eight pipeline stages, 16 prepaid downstream slots) before checking and decoding each beat.
qfd_kvc_decode_map_pc.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_kvc_decode_pc.summary: Per-PC decoder of KV-cache beats landed from HBM; checks expected sector, flags bad beats (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_kvc_decode_pc.about: Physical leaf of the KV stream service's landed-beat decode, one per pseudo-channel. It takes one beat per cycle through four registered stages, compares it with the expected sector/count/window supplied by the PC sequencer and marks invalid beats bad so they can never be written. Credits return only when the downstream FIFO pops.
qfd_kvc_decode_pc.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_link_rx128.summary: Receive-side clock-crossing channel with a 128-word receive buffer on a die link (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_link_rx128.about: The die's credit-based clock-crossing channel configured with a deep 128-word receive buffer, used on a link receive path so the sender can keep a full round trip of words in flight. Order and values are preserved; credit violations raise sticky faults.

qfd_lst_c.summary: Corner link station turning vertical die links east and west (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_lst_c.about: Link-station design in its corner shape: vertical link 0 connects to the west face and link 1 to the east face, each a one-cycle registered stage. The split variant copies one vertical link to both sides and selects the return direction by a static strap.

qfd_lst_h.summary: Link station: registered stage of straight die links on horizontal runs (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_lst_h.about: Same link-station design as qfd_lst_v in the straight shape, placed on horizontal link runs: one-cycle register-to-register delay in both directions for credit-based 512-bit-each-way die links.

qfd_lst_v.summary: Link station: one registered stage of two straight 512-bit-each-way die links (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_lst_v.about: Pure one-cycle delay in both directions for die link bundles (512 data + 16 control bits each way), used along the die's link routes. The link protocol is credit-based end to end, so the station needs no handshake logic. The split variant fans a link to both sides.

qfd_pc_head_owner.summary: Per-PC in-order SRAM queue of pending KV row requests, released on acknowledgements (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_pc_head_owner.about: One per pseudo-channel: holds the PC's queue of KV row requests ('heads', 16 deep, in SECDED-protected SRAM) and releases the current head only when its halves are acknowledged in order, checking for double, unexpected or wrong-PC acknowledgements. Built with every input and output registered at the block boundary.
qfd_pc_head_owner.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_q5_landing_ecc.summary: SECDED-corrects 288-bit KV-cache read data from HBM before it crosses to the core clock (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_q5_landing_ecc.about: Corrects native HBM return data (256 data + 32 check bits) for the KV cache before it enters the core-domain landing FIFO. Each delivery holds a prepaid controller credit until it really retires; an uncorrectable error quarantines that credit instead of reporting success.
qfd_q5_landing_ecc.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_res_ctl.summary: Result-path controller: sequences slot tiles into a conveyor feeding the vector memory (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_res_ctl.about: Control tile of the matrix-engine result path. It drives the slot tiles so requests and responses travel along a registered conveyor, delivering one result row per cycle into the banked vector memory without a global data multiplexer, with credit-based flow control.

qfd_res_slot.summary: Result-path slot tile: buffers matrix-engine result rows in SRAM on the way to vector memory (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_res_slot.about: One slot of the matrix-engine result path, replicated 8 per band. It captures result rows (16 FP32 values plus lane mask) from the band's port slab into its own SRAM macro and metadata, then forwards them as beats toward the banked vector memory.

qfd_rly.summary: Registered relay stage on long die buses, built from the corridor-station design (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_rly.about: A relay instance of the Qwen die station block (one-cycle, register-to-register) inserted on long buses of the die floorplan to break wire length. Values pass through unchanged with a one-cycle delay.

qfd_row_merge_native_fence.summary: Ties the 32 per-PC KV head queues to the row crossbar with a write-before-read fence (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_row_merge_native_fence.about: Binds the 32 per-PC head owners to the KV row arbiter/crossbar and its merge queues. Per PC it enforces the KV write-then-read fence: a head that needs the newest (tail) row of a layer waits until that PC's write of the new position's row is acknowledged, so attention never reads a stale KV row.
qfd_row_merge_native_fence.family: HBM port, ECC and KV-cache path

qfd_seq_su.summary: Sequencer (stream-unit side): fetches the static program and issues ops to the engines (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_seq_su.about: The die's decode sequencer minus the matrix-engine spine and stream unit: it fetches macro-instructions from the program store, adds per-token offsets, and issues them to the matrix engine and stream unit, honouring barriers. It also faces the collective port, KV descriptor path and embedding reads. Variants bi_a/bi_b/boundary_a/boundary_b are alternate cuts.

qfd_seq_su_bi_fea.summary: Variant 'fea' of the stream-unit-side sequencer, with a replicated per-region reset (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_seq_su_bi_fea.about: A variant of the qfd_seq_su sequencer block (program store in SRAM, two-word instruction FIFO head) with its reset release replicated per region. Same function: fetch, offset and issue the static decode program to the engines.

qfd_seq_su_bi_feb.summary: Variant 'feb' of the stream-unit-side sequencer, with a replicated per-region reset (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_seq_su_bi_feb.about: The companion variant to qfd_seq_su_bi_fea of the qfd_seq_su sequencer block (different outline). Same function: fetch, offset and issue the static decode program to the matrix engine and stream unit.

qfd_sp_band_lanes.summary: One band of lanes in the spine reduction tree; sums tile partials and sends band words up (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_sp_band_lanes.about: One band of the matrix engine's spine reduction: it combines the partial sums of the band's positions (tree levels 8-10) and passes the band word to the tree top, with result words going to the slab. Variants (q4, t) are alternate cuts of the same band.
qfd_sp_band_lanes.family: Qwen spine: matrix-engine reduction and result ports

qfd_sp_constants_sequencer_sys.summary: Core controller: program ROM, descriptor ROM, issue logic and tensor-parallel sequencer (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_sp_constants_sequencer_sys.about: The spine's controller block: core fetch/decode/issue (including the argmax fold, engine clock gate and INT8 embedding decode), the tensor-parallel sequencer, the program ROM and the segment-descriptor ROM, with registered stations on its ports.

qfd_sp_constants_sequencer_sys_v_t.summary: Compact-outline variant of the core controller/sequencer block with VM read latency (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_sp_constants_sequencer_sys_v_t.about: A compact-outline variant of qfd_sp_constants_sequencer_sys, the die's controller and tensor-parallel sequencer, extended to account for vector-memory read latency through its stations. Same role: fetch, decode and issue the static decode program.

qfd_sp_su64_sfu.summary: 64-lane vector stream unit with special-function lanes (norms, softmax, SwiGLU) (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_sp_su64_sfu.about: The Qwen ROM die's stream unit: 64 vector lanes, each with its special-function unit, running the element-wise and reduction steps of every layer on data from vector memory. Registered stations on every port separate it from the sequencer, vector memory and matrix engine; the listed variants are alternate floorplans/cuts of the same master.

qfd_sp_vector_memory.summary: Banked vector memory: activation store serving matrix-engine x reads and row ports (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_sp_vector_memory.about: The die's vector memory: activations in row banks of SRAM macros, read for the matrix engine as conflict-free multi-bank beats from a compact stride descriptor, plus row ports for the stream unit and the die link. Variants (bv, bv_t, sq) are alternate outlines/cuts of the same master.

qfd_su64_lane_t.summary: Hardened single lane tile of the 64-lane stream unit, placed 64 times (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_su64_lane_t.about: One lane of the stream unit hardened as its own tile (pin flops in and out, own reset register) and placed 64 times by the SU parent. It holds the lane's pipelined FP32 multiply/add datapath and special-function logic, fed by relayed broadcasts from the SU control.

qfd_su_cbuf_g.summary: 8-lane group of the stream unit's local constant buffer (SRAM + prefetcher), x8 (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_su_cbuf_g.about: One 8-lane group of the SU-local constant buffer: an SRAM macro filled from the die's constant ROM, its lanes' answer pipeline and its own copy of a deterministic prefetcher. Eight copies side by side along the SU face form the full buffer and fill in lockstep, hiding the far constant-ROM latency.

qfd_su_kv624.summary: Packs the stream unit's FP8 K/V values into 624-bit KV-cache write descriptors (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_su_kv624.about: Takes the 64 lanes of K or V values the stream unit has already rounded to FP8 (E4M3) and packs them with a compact address descriptor (K at stride 16, V at stride 1) for the KV-cache write path. Any lane address that does not fit the descriptor suppresses the packet and raises a sticky fault.

qfd_sysctl_stn.summary: Package control plane: host interface, status registers, reset sequencing, die start/done (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_sysctl_stn.about: Control plane of the Qwen ROM package, on die 0 of the TP4 group, in its station/packet-boundary form. It contains the host interface, AXI4-Lite control/status registers with sticky fault collection and interrupts, the reset sequencer (power-on, link training, HBM check, dies ready) and package control that starts all dies on a token and checks they finish and agree.

qfd_tile.summary: Compute tile: ROM weight macros, 8 lane-slice leaves, KV-cache slice and landing hop (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_tile.about: The replicated compute-tile master of the Qwen ROM die (~1,536 copies). It holds ROM macros with the layer weights, eight hardened lane-slice leaves doing the multiply-accumulate, an 8 KiB KV-cache slice, and the per-tile hop of the KV landing fabric that delivers K/V rows to this tile. Activations come down from the spine; partial sums go back to the reduction tree.

qfd_tile_e.summary: Variant of the replicated compute tile (same ROM-tile master, alternate die slot/outline) (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_tile_e.about: A second die-slot variant of the Qwen ROM compute tile built from the same master (ROM macros, eight hardened lane-slice leaves, KV slice and landing hop). It plays the same role as qfd_tile in the token pipeline: weight-stationary matrix-vector work on its ROM rows, with results returned toward the spine.

qfd_tile_lsl.summary: Hardened lane-slice leaf: multiply/accumulate lanes inside each compute tile, 8 per tile (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_tile_lsl.about: The lane-slice leaf of the Qwen ROM compute tile, hardened once and placed eight times in every tile. It multiplies the tile's ROM weight rows by the broadcast activations and accumulates the products through a small adder tree before the tile sends them on to the spine reduction.

qfd_tile_nk.summary: Compute tile variant with no KV-cache slice or landing hop: ROM weights plus lane slices (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_tile_nk.about: A variant of the replicated Qwen ROM compute tile for die slots that hold no KV-cache slice and therefore no landing-fabric hop. It keeps the ROM weight macros and the eight hardened lane-slice leaves that do the matrix-vector multiply-accumulate.

qfd_tt_ctlm.summary: Decode-core control partition: sequencer and controller minus the matrix engine and stream unit (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_tt_ctlm.about: The hardwired decode core with its matrix-engine spine and stream unit removed: the sequencer that fetches the static per-token program, adds per-token offsets (token row, RoPE row, KV slot, context length) and issues operations, plus the controller logic such as the argmax merge. Variants are alternative hardened builds of this partition.

qfd_tt_up4.summary: Upper adder-tree sub-tile: final FP32 reduction levels of the matrix-engine spine, 4 lanes (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_tt_up4.about: Part of the tree top of the matrix-vector engine's reduction spine: it adds the six band words from the band blocks through tree levels 11 and 12 (pipelined FP32 adders) for 4 lanes and returns result words to band 0. Several of these sub-tiles form the full tree top.

qfd_vm_grp.summary: Bank-group tile of the vector memory (SRAM banks + pin flops), 8 per vector memory (Qwen ROM die)
qfd_vm_grp.about: A hardened bank-group tile of the Qwen vector memory, eight of which make up the full VM. Each holds a fixed set of SRAM macros with pin flops on every input, registered outputs, a small FIFO and its own clock tree and reset relay.

qkd_kvwq_ctl.summary: Control tile of the KV write queue: row queue, credits, feeds to PC groups (Qwen KV die)
qkd_kvwq_ctl.about: Captures the posted K/V rows arriving from the ROM die, holds them in a row queue, tracks credits, durability and faults, and feeds each row to the quarter groups of HBM pseudo-channels through registered ports. The binary variant encodes the lane index in binary on the feed.

qkd_kvwq_grp.summary: Quarter-group tile of the KV write queue: drives writes into 8 HBM pseudo-channels (Qwen KV die)
qkd_kvwq_grp.about: One of four quarter-group tiles of the KV-die write queue, serving 8 HBM pseudo-channels on one span of the landing column. It takes feeds from the control tile, checks room and write-done of its PCs, and reports back over registered hops (superseded by the per-PC leaf).

qkd_kvwq_leaf.summary: Per-pseudo-channel leaf of the KV write queue, chained down the landing column (Qwen KV die)
qkd_kvwq_leaf.about: One leaf per HBM pseudo-channel crossing (32 per stack), chained down the landing column. The leaf whose lane matches holds the relayed K/V sector, pushes it when its PC has room, and sends a registered done/bad report back up the chain.
